questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Venous drainage of the thyroid gland
questions.question: Regarding the thyroid gland, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Its isthmus lies on the 3rd to 5th tracheal rings.
options.B: Its lobes are related medially to the carotid sheath.
options.C: Its upper pole is related to the superior laryngeal nerve.
options.D: It is drained by three pairs of veins.

explanations.D: Correct. The thyroid gland is drained by three pairs of veins — superior, middle and inferior thyroid veins. The superior and middle thyroid veins drain into the internal jugular vein, while the inferior thyroid veins descend in front of the trachea to the brachiocephalic veins. Three paired veins therefore carry its venous blood.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The isthmus lies in front of the 2nd, 3rd and 4th tracheal rings, not the 3rd to 5th.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The lobes are related posterolaterally, not medially, to the carotid sheath; medially they relate to the trachea, oesophagus and larynx.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The upper pole and superior thyroid artery are related to the external laryngeal nerve; the superior laryngeal nerve lies higher and more medially.

questions.learning_objective: Venous drainage of the thyroid gland.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Why the thyroid gland moves on swallowing
questions.question: Regarding the thyroid gland, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: It is enclosed by the investing layer of deep fascia.
options.B: It moves up and down with swallowing.
options.C: Its lobes extend up to the hyoid bone.
options.D: The external carotid artery is the only source of its arterial supply.

explanations.B: Correct. The thyroid gland is enclosed by the pretracheal fascia, which binds it to the larynx and trachea, notably through the suspensory ligament of Berry. Because the larynx and trachea rise during deglutition, the gland moves up and down with swallowing. This mobility on swallowing is the classic sign that a midline neck swelling is thyroid in origin.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The false capsule of the gland is derived from the pretracheal, not the investing, layer of deep cervical fascia.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Each lobe extends upward only to the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage, not as high as the hyoid bone.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The gland is supplied by the superior thyroid artery (external carotid) and the inferior thyroid artery (thyrocervical trunk), sometimes with a thyroidea ima; the external carotid is not its only source.

questions.learning_objective: Why the thyroid gland moves on swallowing.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Hoarseness after partial thyroidectomy
questions.question: Following partial thyroidectomy, a patient complained of hoarseness of voice. This is due to injury of which of the following nerves?

explanations.D: Correct. The recurrent laryngeal nerve runs in the tracheo-oesophageal groove behind the gland, close to the inferior thyroid artery, and supplies all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except the cricothyroid. Injury during thyroidectomy paralyses the vocal cord and produces hoarseness. It is the nerve classically injured in partial thyroidectomy.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The superior laryngeal nerve divides into internal and external branches; injury to the whole trunk is uncommon and does not selectively produce cord-paralysis hoarseness.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The internal laryngeal nerve is sensory to the mucosa above the cords; its injury causes loss of the cough reflex and aspiration risk, not hoarseness.
explanations.C: Incorrect. External laryngeal nerve injury weakens the cricothyroid and lowers voice pitch, but the cord is not paralysed, so the voice is not truly hoarse.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Relation of the superior mesenteric vessels to the uncinate process
questions.question: Regarding the pancreas, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The tail passes through the gastrosplenic ligament.
options.B: The superior mesenteric vessels lie anterior to the uncinate process of the head.
options.C: The left renal vein lies anterior to the body.
options.D: The pyloroduodenal junction lies behind the neck.

explanations.B: Correct. The uncinate process is a hook-like extension of the head that projects behind the superior mesenteric vessels. The superior mesenteric artery and vein therefore lie anterior to the uncinate process as they emerge from behind the neck into the mesentery. This relation is why an uncinate carcinoma can encase these vessels.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The tail runs in the splenorenal (lienorenal) ligament, not the gastrosplenic ligament.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The body of the pancreas lies anterior to the left renal vein and left kidney; the vein is posterior, not anterior, to the body.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The neck lies in front of the beginning of the portal vein; the pyloroduodenal junction lies above and in front of the head, not behind the neck.

questions.learning_objective: Relation of the superior mesenteric vessels to the uncinate process.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Upper border of the body of the pancreas
questions.question: Regarding the pancreas, which one of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.A: The common bile duct lies deep to its head.
options.B: Its tail passes through the lienorenal ligament.
options.C: The splenic vein lies along the upper border of its body.

explanations.C: Correct. This is the incorrect statement and therefore the answer. It is the splenic ARTERY that runs a tortuous course along the upper border of the body of the pancreas; the splenic VEIN lies behind the body, below the artery, before joining the superior mesenteric vein to form the portal vein. Placing the splenic vein along the upper border is therefore wrong.
explanations.A: Incorrect. This statement is true: the common bile duct descends in a groove on, or a tunnel through, the posterior surface of the head, deep to it.
explanations.B: Incorrect. This statement is true: the tail is the mobile intraperitoneal part and lies within the lienorenal ligament with the splenic vessels.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This statement is true: except for the tail, the pancreas is a retroperitoneal organ.

questions.learning_objective: Upper border of the body of the pancreas.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Arterial supply of the uncinate process of the pancreas
questions.question: The arterial supply of the uncinate process of the pancreas is derived mainly from the:

explanations.C: Correct. The uncinate process and lower head are supplied mainly by the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery, a branch of the superior mesenteric artery. The upper head is supplied by the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery from the gastroduodenal branch of the coeliac trunk, and the two form an anastomotic arcade. Because the uncinate lies against the superior mesenteric vessels, its dominant supply is the SMA.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The coeliac trunk supplies the upper head/neck indirectly through the gastroduodenal and superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries, not the uncinate process directly.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The splenic artery supplies the neck, body and tail, not the uncinate process.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The inferior mesenteric artery supplies the hindgut and has no pancreatic branches.

questions.learning_objective: Arterial supply of the uncinate process of the pancreas.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Duodenal obstruction in annular pancreas
questions.question: A 4-year-old boy was admitted with severe vomiting; investigations revealed an annular pancreas. Which of the following structures is most typically obstructed in this condition?

explanations.C: Correct. In annular pancreas a ring of pancreatic tissue encircles the descending (second) part of the duodenum, at the site where the ventral bud normally rotates. Constriction of this segment produces duodenal obstruction with vomiting in infancy. The second part of the duodenum is therefore the classically obstructed site.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The pylorus lies proximal to the ring and is not encircled by the annular tissue.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The first part (duodenal cap) lies above the ampullary level and the pancreatic ring.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The third part is crossed by the superior mesenteric vessels but is not the segment encircled by an annular pancreas.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Embryological origin of the thyroid gland
questions.question: Regarding the development of the thyroid gland, choose the correct statement:

options.A: The thyroglossal duct remains patent after birth.
options.B: During its descent it passes behind the thyroid cartilage.
options.C: It is derived from the floor of the pharynx.
options.D: The thyroid follicles are mesodermal in origin.

explanations.C: Correct. The thyroid gland develops from a median endodermal downgrowth of the floor of the primitive pharynx, at the site later marked by the foramen cecum of the tongue. This median thyroid diverticulum descends in the neck to its pretracheal position. Its follicular cells are therefore endodermal derivatives of the pharyngeal floor.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The thyroglossal duct normally atrophies and disappears in the fetus; persistence is abnormal and produces cysts or fistulae.
explanations.B: Incorrect. During descent the gland passes in front of the hyoid and laryngeal cartilages, not behind them.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The thyroid follicles are endodermal, not mesodermal, in origin.

questions.learning_objective: Embryological origin of the thyroid gland.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Anterior relation of the head of the pancreas
questions.question: Regarding the head of the pancreas, choose the correct statement:

options.A: It lies in the left hypochondrium.
options.B: It is related anteriorly to the transverse colon.
options.C: It is covered completely by the peritoneum.
options.D: It is related posteriorly to loops of small intestine.

explanations.B: Correct. The head of the pancreas lies within the concavity of the duodenum and is crossed anteriorly by the attachment of the transverse mesocolon and the transverse colon, with coils of jejunum below. Above the mesocolon its anterior surface is related to the pylorus. The transverse colon is therefore a correct anterior relation of the head.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The head lies in the epigastrium within the duodenal C-loop; it is the tail that reaches the left hypochondrium.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The pancreas is retroperitoneal, covered by peritoneum only on its anterior surface, not completely.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Posteriorly the head is related to the inferior vena cava, right renal vessels, bile duct and aorta, not to loops of small intestine.

questions.learning_objective: Anterior relation of the head of the pancreas.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Venous bleeding during emergency tracheostomy
questions.question: During an emergency tracheostomy through a midline incision below the isthmus, profuse dark venous bleeding suddenly occurred. Which vessel was most likely injured?

explanations.C: Correct. Below the isthmus, in the midline in front of the trachea, lie the inferior thyroid veins (often a plexus, with an occasional thyroidea ima vein) descending to the left brachiocephalic vein. A low midline tracheostomy incision passes over these veins, producing dark venous bleeding. They are the vessels classically cut in this approach.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The superior thyroid vein accompanies the superior thyroid artery at the upper pole, away from a low midline incision.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The middle thyroid vein runs laterally from the lobe to the internal jugular vein, not in the infra-isthmic midline.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The external jugular vein lies superficially over the sternocleidomastoid, lateral to a midline tracheostomy incision.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Midline neck cyst that moves on tongue protrusion
questions.question: A 7-year-old presented with a mobile mass in the anterior midline of the neck that elevated on protrusion of the tongue. This cyst most likely developed from which embryonic structure?

explanations.D: Correct. A thyroglossal cyst arises from a persistent remnant of the thyroglossal duct, the tract along which the thyroid descended from the foramen cecum of the tongue. Because the tract stays attached to the hyoid and tongue base, the cyst rises when the tongue is protruded — the diagnostic sign. Its midline position and this movement identify it as a thyroglossal duct remnant.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The first pharyngeal cleft forms the external acoustic meatus; its remnants present near the ear.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The first pharyngeal pouch forms the tubotympanic recess (middle ear and auditory tube), not a midline neck cyst.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Second-cleft remnants form lateral (branchial) cysts along the sternocleidomastoid and do not move with tongue protrusion.

questions.learning_objective: Midline neck cyst that moves on tongue protrusion.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Formation of the main pancreatic duct
questions.question: The main pancreatic duct (of Wirsung) is formed of:

options.C: The whole dorsal pancreatic duct and the whole ventral pancreatic duct.
options.D: The distal part of the dorsal pancreatic duct and the duct of the ventral pancreas.

explanations.D: Correct. The main pancreatic duct forms by fusion of the entire duct of the ventral bud with the distal part of the dorsal bud duct. The proximal part of the dorsal duct persists as the accessory duct of Santorini. This mixed origin is why the main duct opens with the bile duct at the major papilla while the accessory duct opens at the minor papilla.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The dorsal duct contributes only its distal part; its proximal part becomes the accessory duct, so "dorsal only" is wrong.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The ventral duct alone drains only the ventral derivatives; the main duct also incorporates the distal dorsal duct.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Only the distal, not the whole, dorsal duct joins the ventral duct; the proximal dorsal duct becomes the accessory duct of Santorini.

questions.learning_objective: Formation of the main pancreatic duct.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Lymphatic drainage of the pancreas
questions.question: Regarding the pancreas, which one of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.A: Its lymph vessels drain into both the superior and inferior mesenteric nodes.
options.B: The inferior vena cava lies behind the head of the pancreas.
options.C: The tail lies within the lienorenal ligament.
options.D: The beginning of the portal vein lies deep to the neck.

explanations.A: Correct. This is the incorrect statement and therefore the answer. Pancreatic lymph drains to the pancreaticosplenic, coeliac and superior mesenteric (and hepatic/pyloric) nodes; it does not drain to the inferior mesenteric nodes, which serve the hindgut. Claiming drainage into the inferior mesenteric nodes is therefore wrong.
explanations.B: Incorrect. This statement is true: the inferior vena cava is a posterior relation of the head of the pancreas.
explanations.C: Incorrect. This statement is true: the tail is intraperitoneal within the lienorenal ligament with the splenic vessels.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This statement is true: the neck lies in front of the beginning of the portal vein, formed behind it by the splenic and superior mesenteric veins.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Medial extent of the left suprarenal gland
questions.question: Regarding the suprarenal glands, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The left gland is drained into the I.V.C.
options.B: The left gland is related anteriorly to the head of the pancreas.
options.C: Each gland receives four suprarenal arteries.
options.D: The left gland reaches the hilum of the kidney.

explanations.D: Correct. The left suprarenal gland is semilunar and larger than the right, extending down the medial border of the left kidney to reach the region of the renal hilum. Its lower pole is closely related to the hilar vessels. The left gland reaching the hilum of the kidney is therefore the correct statement.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The left suprarenal vein drains into the left renal vein, not directly into the IVC; it is the right suprarenal vein that opens into the IVC.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The left gland is related anteriorly to the body/tail of the pancreas and the stomach bed, not to the head of the pancreas.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Each suprarenal gland receives three arteries — superior (inferior phrenic), middle (aorta) and inferior (renal artery) — not four.

questions.learning_objective: Medial extent of the left suprarenal gland.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Blood supply of the posterior lobe of the pituitary
questions.question: Regarding the pituitary gland, choose the correct answer:

options.A: It consists of a small anterior lobe and a large posterior lobe.
options.B: It is related posteriorly to the medulla oblongata.
options.C: The posterior lobe is supplied by the inferior hypophyseal artery inside the cavernous sinus.
options.D: A pituitary tumour causes binasal hemianopia due to pressure on the optic chiasma.

explanations.C: Correct. The inferior hypophyseal artery, a branch of the internal carotid artery within the cavernous sinus, supplies the posterior lobe (neurohypophysis) directly. The anterior lobe instead receives blood indirectly through the hypothalamo-hypophyseal portal system from the superior hypophyseal arteries. So the posterior lobe has a direct arterial supply from the inferior hypophyseal artery.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The anterior lobe (adenohypophysis) is the larger part and the posterior lobe the smaller; the sizes are reversed here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The gland lies in the hypophyseal fossa related posteriorly to the dorsum sellae, not to the medulla oblongata.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Chiasmatic compression by a pituitary tumour classically causes a bitemporal, not binasal, hemianopia by compressing the crossing nasal retinal fibres.

questions.learning_objective: Blood supply of the posterior lobe of the pituitary.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Zonation of the suprarenal cortex
questions.question: Regarding the suprarenal glands, choose the correct answer:

options.A: The cortex is divided into three zones — zona glomerulosa, zona fasciculata and zona reticularis, from superficial to deep.
options.B: The suprarenal cortex is ectodermal in origin.
options.C: The suprarenal medulla is mesodermal in origin.
options.D: The hilum of the left suprarenal gland is directed upwards.

explanations.A: Correct. The suprarenal cortex has three concentric zones from the capsule inward: zona glomerulosa (mineralocorticoids), zona fasciculata (glucocorticoids) and zona reticularis (androgens), i.e. superficial to deep. This is the correct description of cortical zonation. The medulla lies deep to the reticularis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The cortex is mesodermal in origin, from coelomic mesothelium, not ectodermal.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The medulla is ectodermal, derived from neural-crest chromaffin cells, not mesodermal.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The hilum of the left suprarenal gland is directed downward and medially toward the renal vessels, not upward.

questions.subject: endo
questions.title: Ligation of the inferior thyroid artery in thyroidectomy
questions.question: Regarding the thyroid gland, which one of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.A: The posterior surface of the thyroid lobe is related to the medial part of the carotid sheath.
options.B: Ligation of the inferior thyroid artery should be as near as possible to the gland.
options.C: The inferior thyroid artery is a branch of the thyrocervical trunk of the first part of the subclavian artery.
options.D: The inferior thyroid vein drains into the brachiocephalic vein.

explanations.B: Correct. This is the incorrect statement and therefore the answer. The inferior thyroid artery should be ligated well away from the gland, in continuity and laterally, because near the gland it is intimately related to the recurrent laryngeal nerve and would endanger it; the superior thyroid artery, by contrast, is ligated close to the gland to spare the external laryngeal nerve. Ligating the inferior thyroid artery near the gland is therefore wrong.
explanations.A: Incorrect. This statement is true: the posteromedial aspect of the lobe is related to the carotid sheath and its contents.
explanations.C: Incorrect. This statement is true: the inferior thyroid artery arises from the thyrocervical trunk, a branch of the first part of the subclavian artery.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This statement is true: the inferior thyroid veins drain into the brachiocephalic (innominate) veins.

questions.learning_objective: Ligation of the inferior thyroid artery in thyroidectomy.
